speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: asked the Minister for Education in light of the 2023 Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey, whether the Ministry plans to (i) discover why, when compared with their university peers, the arts, design and media graduates have poorer employment and salary outcomes and the health sciences graduates have poorer salary outcomes (ii) engage graduates of such courses on how to improve their employment outcomes and (iii) engage the relevant sector agencies and stakeholders to take steps to narrow the employment and salary outcome gap.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This is reflective of the economic demand and the labour market conditions of each sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and DesignSingapore Council (Dsg) have also been working closely with the universities and key industry partners to provide our graduates with a good education and relevant, in-demand skill sets to take on good jobs and thrive in the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Dsg also facilitates partnerships between universities and companies, such as through the Design Education Advisory Committee, to enhance industry exposure and internship opportunities for our students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: To support all students and graduates as they enter the workforce, our universities organise career fairs and have career coaches to provide mentoring and workshops.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Graduates can also approach Workforce Singapore's Careers Connect or NTUC's e2i career centres, if they require support in their job search.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: At the same time, we encourage our students to consider longer-term factors, such as career progression, salary and growth opportunities in the sector, as they pursue their passion and decide on the course of study in the universities.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The first is relating to arts and design.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: I do understand that if we look at arts and design as a vertical skill, then in terms of opportunities, it is quite confined.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: But I just would like to follow up on some of the mentions in my previous Budget speech.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Looking at the growth of various sectors, such as tourism, entertainment and so forth; in Singapore, where, in terms of growth potential and economic opportunities are much more, what would be the steps taken to integrate these creative arts professionals in these fields, with these growth industries?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Second, for health sciences, I also do understand that there is a big push for Healthier SG.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: What are the opportunity spaces in which the schools are looking at to bridge these graduates with the opportunities on-stream?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For the arts and design graduates, just for Member's information, they do not just go to arts and design jobs.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: So, indeed, in our education, we hope to equip our students with both broad-based as well as vertical skill sets, so that they have more opportunities and career choices when they graduate.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For health sciences, yes, Healthier SG is an exciting development.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) will work very closely with MOH to make sure that the curriculum and the skills frameworks are updated so that our students will have maximal opportunities when they graduate.
